newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-AUSTRALIAN GENERAL NEWS - AUG 12.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-AUSTRALIAN GENERAL NEWS - AUG 12.

text.p: THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Twenty-six private Australian companies presented their businesses to the region's leading venture capital investors in Singapore last week, as Australia's capital gains tax and a lack of start-up investment drives some of Australia's most ambitious small companies to seek funds from the new money managers in Asia. Page 1.

The New South Wales and South Australian Governments are resisting a plan by the other States to avoid alcohol price rises by giving back pre-paid liquor licensing fees. Victoria, Queensland, the Australian Capital Territory and Tasmania have agreed to remburse the fees, but a crisis meeting of State officials in Sydney yesterday ended in deadlock. Page 3.

A new media ownership model based on the British system, and retaining the current cross-media ownership limits, is expected to be considered by Federal Cabinet today. Media proprietors, however, will now be able to argue specific cases under a public benefit test administered by the Australian Broadcasting Authority. The changes could allow Kerry Packer to buy John Fairfax Holdings while still retaining Nine. Page 3.

Federal Opposition Leader Kim Beazley has told his ministry that he will not replace shadow ministers Carmen Lawrence, Senator Bob Collins and Peter Baldwin, who are all standing down. Beazley is seeking to appoint backbench taskforces to help assess newcomers, and to involve them in the Parliament. Page 5.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Australia yesterday offered to loan A$1.35 billion to Thailand at a meeting in Tokyo organised by the International Monetary Fund to put together a US$16 billion rescue package for Thailand's troubled economy. Australia's offer doubled from the original U$500 million after it was learnt a number of Asian countries would each lend US$1 billion. Page 1.

Federal Treasurer Peter Costello last night called on New South Wales, Western Australia and South Australia to follow the lead of the other States and reimburse the liquor industry for pre-paid licence fees so that alcohol prices do not increase. Costell stopped short of threatening to withhold funds from States that do not refund the fees. Page 1.

Barrister John Lee told the Victorian Supreme Court yesterday that the discovery of missing toddler Jaidyn Leskie's soiled clothes and toys by the boy's mother, while the man accused with his murder, Greg Domaszewicz, was in custody suggests someone else had access to Leskie or his body. Domaszewicz was refused bail however, because no exceptional circumstances were shown. Page 1.

Prime Minister John Howard will chair a Cabinet meeting today which is expected to endorse an overhaul of the Federal Government's industry policy to make it more effective in attracting new international investment to the country, without undermining the Government's tight Budget strategy. Page 1.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

A proposal for a billion dollar fund to promote foreign investment in Australia, backed by Federal Industries Minister John Moore, is likely to be resisted by other Cabinet Ministers at a Federal Cabinet meeting on industry policy today. The debate will determine how far the Government is willing to go to adapt to suit business. Page 1.

The Federal Government has doubled its proposed offer of US$500 million as part of the International Monetary Fund's rescue package for the Thai economy after Federal Foreign Affairs Minister Alexander Downer told Cabinet yesterday that, in the national iterest, the loan should match those of other regional contributors. Page 1.

The town of Helidon, 100 kilometres west of Brisbane, has been overrun by members of the Catholic sect called the "Magnificat Meal Movement". Hundreds flock to the town to hear the words of Movement leader Debra Geileskey, who claims to speak to God ever day. Geileskey plans to build a A$40 million basilica in the town to seat a congregation of 7000. Page 1.

Australia Post has proposed a five-year freeze on the price of a postage stamp at 45 cents, increased business discounts, and the introduction of new technology, in return for a more gradual deregulation of letter delivery instead of the radical changes called for by several courier companies. Page 3.
THE AGE

The Australian cricket team yesterday defeated England in the fifth Ashes Test match, thereby retaining the Ashes and becoming the first team to win five successive Ashes series. England only managed 186 runs in their chase of a target of 451. Page 1.

Victorian Treasurer Alan Stockdale has announced the State Government will refund more than A$40 million in pre-paid liquor licence fees. The move follows a warning from hoteliers that they would be forced to increase alcohol prices to compensate for the new Federal tax which resulted from the High Court's ruling invalidating the States' powers to tax alcohol, tobacco and fuel. Page 1.

The mother of missing toddler Jaidyn Leskie, Bilynda Murphy, told the Supreme Court yesterday that she did not believe her boyfriend, Greg Domaszewicz, had murdered her child, despite an earlier letter in which she had accused him of murdering the 14-month-old. Justice Bill Gillard refused Domaszewicz bail. Page 1.

Federal Treasurer Peter Costello last night announced that Australia would take part in an International Monetary Fund rescue package for Thailand by lending A$1.3 billion. The original commitment was doubled after Federal Foreign Affairs Minister Alexaner Downer argued that Australia should match the contributions of other nations. Page 3.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
